summary: Dashboard permissioning: add 'Restricted' visibility model for customer-specific Dedicated SLO/error-budget views
description:
Request
We need a standard permissioning pattern for customer-specific Dedicated dashboards (SLO + burn rate + pool readiness) that are generated from the same templates as internal dashboards but must not be broadly visible.

Background
As part of the Tiered SLO + Error Budget program, we are building Dedicated-tier dashboards that can be shared with specific customers (via CSM/Support or in a customer-facing view). These dashboards include customer identifiers (account_id / dedicated_pool_id) and should be treated as Restricted.

Problem
Current Grafana folder permissions are too coarse:
- SRE/Platform engineers need broad access for oncall and debugging.
- Support/CS needs view-only access for escalations, but should not be able to browse all Dedicated customers.
- Most employees should not be able to discover or access customer-specific Dedicated dashboards.

Requirements / Proposed approach
1) Add a 'Restricted' folder class for Grafana/Observability:
   - Folder naming convention: "Dedicated - Restricted - <CustomerCompany> (<account_id>)"
   - Default: not visible to org-wide viewers.

2) Define access groups and mapping:
   - rwd-observability-admins: full admin (existing)
   - rwd-sre-oncall: Viewer + folder access to all Restricted folders
   - rwd-platform-oncall: Viewer + folder access to all Restricted folders
   - rwd-customer-ops-l2 (Support/CS escalation): Viewer access only to a customer folder when ticket escalated (per-customer grant)
   - rwd-csm-<customer>: Viewer access to that customer's folder only (optional; not for MVP)

3) Audit + operational workflow
   - All per-customer grants must be time-bounded (suggest 14d) unless explicitly approved.
   - Maintain an audit trail: who granted access, when, and justification (link to SUP-* ticket).
   - Add runbook snippet: how Support requests access + expected turnaround.

4) Guardrails
   - Prevent dashboard variables from allowing cross-customer data exploration (e.g., avoid global account pickers in Restricted views).
   - Ensure panels cannot query non-scoped datasources that bypass label-based scoping.

Acceptance criteria
- A Restricted folder can be created and is not visible to default 'All Employees' Grafana role.
- SRE/Platform oncall can access all Restricted folders without manual intervention.
- Support can be granted view-only access to a single customer folder, time-bounded, with an audit note containing a SUP-* reference.
- Documented procedure is available for Support + SRE (short, operational).

Notes / urgency
We have active Dedicated escalations asking for "what does Redwood see" for SLOs/error budgets (SUP-3950). We need this before we start routinely sharing Dedicated SLO views during incidents and QBRs.

Requested by
- Sergio Costa (Dashboards)
- Felix Schneider (Customer-facing SLO dashboard backend)

Owner suggestions
Telemetry/Observability (Logan) with Console input for future in-product views.

Attachments/links
- Dashboard templates landing in observability-pack PR #77
- Confluence naming/structure: SLO Dashboards Structure & Naming
- Tiered SLO definitions: Hosted vs Dedicated
